userStories.title: Classify and stamp terminal advisory recurrence
acceptanceCriteria: classifyRecurrence returns an object carrying retired and classified arrays in addition to blocking, advisory, and demoted arrays.
Given a warning finding, an error threshold, and fewer prior fingerprint appearances than maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence places it in advisory and not retired.
Given a sub-threshold finding whose fingerprint appearance count including the current round is at or above maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence places it in retired and not advisory.
Given an error-severity finding whose appearance count including the current round is at or above maxBlockingRounds + 1, classifyRecurrence places it in demoted and not retired.
When cfg omits maxAdvisoryRounds and a sub-threshold finding reaches appearance count 2, classifyRecurrence places it in retired using the documented default.
Every finding in classified carries meta.recurrence.disposition equal to the bucket name blocking, advisory, demoted, or retired that received it.
A finding in demoted carries meta.recurrence.wasBlocking equal to true.
A finding in retired carries meta.recurrence.wasBlocking equal to false.
Every finding in classified carries meta.recurrence.rounds equal to its prior appearance count plus one.
classified contains one entry per input finding in input order.
When an input finding has no meta, classifyRecurrence does not mutate it and it still has no meta after the call.
When an input finding carries an unrelated meta key, its classified entry retains that key alongside meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence returns an empty retired array.
When cfg.enabled is false, no finding returned by classifyRecurrence carries meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence partitions findings into blocking and advisory by severity exactly as before and returns classified as the unchanged input array.
When priorIterations is empty, classifyRecurrence returns an empty retired array.
When priorIterations is empty, every classified entry carries meta.recurrence.rounds equal to 1.
Given a finding without acIndex, classifyRecurrence uses the existing file, category, and issue-prefix fingerprint fallback and its disposition stamping remains unaffected.
Given a test-gap finding in a matching test file at or above the blocking threshold, classifyRecurrence places it in blocking regardless of appearance count.
Given a test-gap finding in a matching test file below the blocking threshold, classifyRecurrence does not place it in blocking.
When adversarial review config omits recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds, schema parsing resolves it to 2.
When semantic review config omits recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds, schema parsing resolves it to 2.
When semantic review config omits recurrenceDemotion.enabled, schema parsing resolves it to false.
When either review config sets recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds to 0, schema validation rejects it.
When tagCoverageGap is applied to a finding carrying meta.recurrence, it returns a finding carrying that meta.recurrence and meta.coverageGap equal to true.

routing.reasoning: The algorithm changes a shared generic result contract and behavior across recurrence, schemas, types, and default assertions; isolated test and implementation sessions reduce regression risk.

outOfScope: The wording of the reviewer prompt; the `meta.coverageGap` tag's own semantics, which are unchanged.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test at `:6-9` asserts `expect(parsed.recurrenceDemotion).toEqual({ enabled: true, maxBlockingRounds: 2 })`, and `:10-15` makes the same exact-object assertion for the override case. `toEqual` is exact, so the schema's new `maxAdvisoryRounds` default fails both against a correct implementation. US-001 owns updating them to the new invariant: the parsed object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

the assertion at `:113` pins `result.data.review.semantic` with `toEqual`, including a nested `recurrenceDemotion: { enabled: false, maxBlockingRounds: 2 }`. The new schema default breaks it against a correct implementation. US-001 owns updating it to the new invariant: the nested object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

userStories.title: Propagate recurrence verdicts through review outputs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve recurrence stamps through LLM-to-Finding conversion and expose classified raw findings in review audit output.

**Motivation** — a passing record can carry an `error` finding with no explanation.

**Approach** — Both LLM finding types gain an optional `meta`, and both mappers gain one allowlist line forwarding `recurrence`.

The `result.findings` lane needs no mapper at all: per `semantic-helpers.ts:61-62` and #1861, the review audit persists the **raw op shape**, so a stamp on the LLM finding reaches `ReviewAuditEntry.result.findings` directly through `review-decision.ts:92`. That is the nax#1928 evidence surface, and it comes free.

**Scope** — In: LLM finding metadata, mapper allowlists, classified operation findings, retired advisory folding, retirement telemetry. Out: recurrence classification/schema work (US-001); prompt rendering and fix-lane filtering (US-003); Changing how `passed` is computed at `adversarial-review.ts:512`. A record carrying `passed: true` beside a demoted `error` keeps that verdict and explains it.; Enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review. The schema field is wired, the default stays `false`, and flipping it is a separate decision needing its own baseline.

**Interface** — `AdversarialLLMFinding` and the semantic `LLMFinding` each gain `meta?: Record<string, unknown>`. `toAdversarialReviewFindings` and `llmFindingToFinding` each gain one allowlist line forwarding `f.meta?.recurrence` into `metaExtras`, alongside the existing `evidence` line. The review operations persist `classified` as `findings` and fold `retired` into `advisoryFindings`.
acceptanceCriteria: When toAdversarialReviewFindings converts an LLM finding carrying meta.recurrence, the Finding meta.recurrence preserves disposition, rounds, and wasBlocking values.
When toAdversarialReviewFindings converts an LLM finding with no meta, the Finding meta has no recurrence key.
When toAdversarialReviewFindings converts an LLM finding carrying meta.recurrence and verifiedBy, the Finding carries both meta.recurrence and meta.verifiedBy.
When llmFindingToFinding converts a semantic LLM finding carrying meta.recurrence, the Finding meta.recurrence preserves disposition, rounds, and wasBlocking values.
When adversarialReviewOp.verify() accepts findings, its findings output contains one stamped meta.recurrence.disposition entry per accepted finding.
When adversarialReviewOp.verify() classifies entries as retired, advisoryFindings contains those entries in addition to the advisory, demoted, and AC-dropped entries it already carries.
adversarialReviewOp.verify() returns normalizedFindings containing only blocking-classified entries, so a retired finding is never routable to the rectification cycle.

Given a warning finding and matching priorAdversarialIterations sufficient to reach maxAdvisoryRounds, adversarialReviewOp.verify() returns that finding inside advisoryFindings stamped meta.recurrence.disposition retired.

When classifyRecurrence returns a non-empty retired array, adversarialReviewOp.verify() emits one info-level review log record per retired finding with event review.adversarial.recurrence_retired and the finding's file and category.
When classifyRecurrence returns demoted findings, adversarialReviewOp.verify() still emits one log record per demoted finding with event review.adversarial.recurrence_demoted.
When semanticReviewOp.verify() has recurrenceDemotion.enabled true, its findings output contains one stamped meta.recurrence.disposition entry per accepted finding.
When semanticReviewOp.verify() uses recurrenceDemotion.enabled false by default, its advisoryFindings entries carry no meta.recurrence.

Given an adversarial verify output whose findings carry meta.recurrence, when the review-audit entry is built, result.findings exposes those values so a reader of a passed true record can distinguish a demoted error from a miscomputed verdict without replaying demotion state.

When an error-severity finding is classified demoted and blocking is empty, adversarialReviewOp.verify() returns passed true, so the verdict rule at adversarial-review.ts:512 is unchanged by this feature.

routing.reasoning: This is a bounded propagation change across five existing seams with established mapper and verify-test patterns, and no new abstraction or concurrency.

outOfScope: The computation of `passed`; enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review, whose default stays `false`.

userStories.title: Render retired findings as closed and exclude their fix seeds
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move retired findings out of mandatory prior-review verdicts and prevent them from starting non-blocking fixes.

**Motivation** — The only way to stop a reviewer re-raising a true finding is to keep telling it about the finding.

**Approach** — So retirement is a **rendering** change: the finding stays in the store and stays in the prompt, but moves out of the verdict list — which requires a per-item classification and mandates identical re-flagging — into an acknowledgement block that states it is closed and must not be re-flagged. The reviewer keeps the memory; the prompt stops asking for the re-emission.

`buildPriorIterationsBlock` partitions each iteration's findings by `meta.recurrence.disposition`. Entries stamped `retired` render in a separate acknowledgement section stating they are closed and must not be re-flagged; every other entry renders as today. The verdict template counts only the non-retired entries.

`actionableAdvisoryFindings` additionally drops entries stamped `meta.recurrence.disposition === "retired"`. This is a seeding-site filter, matching that function's own documented convention. Without it a retired finding buys an agent session — the system would pay to fix what it just declared closed.

**Scope** — In: prompt rendering partition/count and advisory seed filtering. Out: recurrence stamping and mapper/operation propagation (US-001 and US-002); Changing the `still-blocking` instruction at `prior-iterations-builder.ts:115`. Retirement works by moving a finding out of the verdict list, not by softening the instruction that governs the list.; Dropping retired findings from the iteration store or from `advisoryFindings`. They remain stored and remain reported; only their prompt rendering and their fix-lane eligibility change.; Excluding `acDropped` findings from the non-blocking-fix seed. That filter at `non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60` is an existing hold on nax#1801 and is left exactly as it stands.

**Interface** — `buildPriorIterationsBlock<F extends Finding>(iterations: Iteration<F>[]): string` renders retired findings in an acknowledgement block and excludes them from the verdict-required total. `actionableAdvisoryFindings(findings: readonly Finding[]): readonly Finding[]` omits findings whose `meta.recurrence.disposition === "retired"`.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an iteration containing a finding stamped meta.recurrence.disposition retired, buildPriorIterationsBlock omits that finding from its verdict-required list.
Given that iteration, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns an acknowledgement section naming the retired finding's file and category.
Given retired findings in the acknowledgement section, the section states they are closed and must not be re-flagged, so the still-blocking instruction does not apply to them.
Given an iteration whose findings carry no meta.recurrence, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns a block identical to the one it returns today, so rounds recorded before this feature render unchanged.
buildPriorIterationsBlock's verdict template counts only findings not stamped retired.
Given an iteration whose findings are all stamped retired, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns a block containing no verdict-required list.

Given three consecutive review rounds where a warning finding is emitted in round 1 and reaches maxAdvisoryRounds in round 2, the prior-iterations block built for round 3 lists that finding only in the acknowledgement section.
Given a finding stamped meta.recurrence.disposition retired, actionableAdvisoryFindings returns a list omitting it.
Given a finding stamped meta.recurrence.disposition advisory, actionableAdvisoryFindings returns a list containing it.
actionableAdvisoryFindings continues to omit findings whose actionRequired is false and findings whose acDropped is true.
When execution planning receives advisory findings whose only entries are retired, shouldRunNonBlockingFix receives an advisory count excluding retired findings and dispatches no fix pass.

routing.reasoning: The work is limited to existing prompt and advisory-seeding functions plus their wiring, with clear observable output and dispatch behavior.

outOfScope: The run-end advisory report surface, which continues to read `advisoryFindings` and therefore still lists retired findings.

modifiedFiles.reason: assertions over the rendered block's finding count and its verdict template. Under AC 1 and AC 5 a retired entry leaves the verdict list and the template count drops accordingly, so any count-based expectation over a fixture containing a stamped entry fails against a correct implementation. US-003 owns updating them to the new invariant: the verdict list and its template count only entries not stamped `disposition: "retired"`, and retired entries appear once in the acknowledgement section.

analysis:
Existing recurrence classification is the primary change seam: it currently returns only blocking/advisory/demoted, computes recurrence only after a sub-threshold early return, and mutates neither input nor metadata (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:137-216`). Preserve its fingerprint identity, mixed AC/prose lookup, per-prior-iteration counting, and blocking-only test-gap carve-out (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:61-131, 172-216`). The new stamp must be immutable and merge unrelated metadata. Disabled recurrence must preserve the legacy severity partition and return classified as the unchanged input array; absent maxAdvisoryRounds must resolve to 2 inside classification.

Schema defaults exist separately for semantic and adversarial review (`src/config/schemas-review.ts:77-82, 135-140`) and the parallel optional inline config shapes are in `src/review/types.ts:132, 258`. Existing exact-object schema/default tests must be updated for the added resolved field (`test/unit/config/schemas-review.test.ts:5-15`; `test/unit/config/semantic-review.test.ts:36-113,258`). The LLM mapper boundaries reconstruct `meta` from closed allowlists (`src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:136-166`; `src/review/semantic-helpers.ts:188-209`), so both LLM types need optional meta and both mappers must forward recurrence explicitly. `tagCoverageGap` already merges metadata after conversion and must retain that behavior (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:133-135`).

Both operations classify accepted raw findings but currently expose raw accepted findings and only convert blocking/advisory/demoted buckets (`src/operations/adversarial-review.ts:479-539`; `src/operations/semantic-review.ts:425-470`). They must expose classified raw findings to audit, keep normalizedFindings blocking-only, fold retired into advisoryFindings, and log adversarial retirement. `review-decision` already forwards record.findings directly into result.findings (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/review-decision.ts:89-93`), so it needs no code change.

Retirement must be a prompt rendering partition, not store removal. The prior-iteration builder currently renders and counts every findingsAfter entry (`src/prompts/builders/prior-iterations-builder.ts:47-127`); partition retired entries per iteration, render their file/category in a closed/do-not-re-flag acknowledgement section, and count only visible verdict entries. Historic entries without recurrence metadata must retain current rendering. The centralized NBF seed filter (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60`) feeds the dispatch count in execution planning (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:396-408`), so filtering retired there prevents an agent pass while keeping advisory reporting intact.

Compatibility risks are public result-shape expansion, accidental raw finding mutation, metadata loss at conversion, schema exact-object regressions, and disabled-mode stamps. Implement in dependency order: classification/config; mapper and operation propagation; rendering and NBF filtering. No persisted-data migration is required: older iteration findings without recurrence metadata remain verdict-required and new findings remain stored and reported.
outOfScope: The nax#1910 step-3 analyzer over `review-audit/*.json` — measured 2026-09-10 at 11.1% `unmatched` on 27 sub-threshold findings from a single feature, too small a sample to justify building it.

Retiring a finding on `meta.evidence.status === "unmatched"`. All three `unmatched` findings in the measured corpus were substantive defects, so evidence status measures quote hygiene rather than finding validity and must not gate retirement.
Seeding the non-blocking-fix lane from semantic-review's advisory bucket, tracked as nax#1957 and gated on the nax#1801 ruling.
Changing how `passed` is computed at `adversarial-review.ts:512`. A record carrying `passed: true` beside a demoted `error` keeps that verdict and explains it.
Enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review. The schema field is wired, the default stays `false`, and flipping it is a separate decision needing its own baseline.
The "whack-a-mole within a file" failure where each round yields genuinely new findings, tracked as nax#1157.
Excluding `acDropped` findings from the non-blocking-fix seed. That filter at `non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60` is an existing hold on nax#1801 and is left exactly as it stands.
Changing the `still-blocking` instruction at `prior-iterations-builder.ts:115`. Retirement works by moving a finding out of the verdict list, not by softening the instruction that governs the list.
Similarity-clustering or otherwise changing `fingerprintFor`. Retirement inherits whatever recurrence identity that function already provides.
Dropping retired findings from the iteration store or from `advisoryFindings`. They remain stored and remain reported; only their prompt rendering and their fix-lane eligibility change.
